mainTopic: The order of the morning עבודה: bringing the coals, the פסכתר, the signal of the מגרפה, and the jobs inside the היכל ending with the burning of the קטורת.
overview: This amud has no back-and-forth argument. It is plain משנה describing the order of the morning עבודה in the מקדש. First it finishes describing the קטורת vessel. Then the כהן of the מחתה scoops coals from the outer מזבח with a silver pan and pours them into a gold pan. The spilled coals are swept into the אמה, but on שבת they are covered with the פסכתר, which had three uses. Next, a כהן throws the מגרפה, and its loud sound signals the כהנים, the לוים, and the ראש המעמד, and the פרק ends. The new פרק הֵחֵלּוּ עוֹלִים describes each כהן's job inside the היכל: the inner מזבח, the מנורה, spreading the coals, and burning the קטורת only when the ממונה gives the word. The פרק ends with the people stepping away while the קטורת is burned.

steps.title: The incense vessel was heaped full and covered
steps.stepSummary: The previous משנה ends by describing the incense vessel. It was heaped with קטורת, had a lid, and had a cloth spread over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was full and heaped with incense. It had a lid, and a kind of cloth was spread over it on top.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing its description of the vessel holding the קטורת, which began in the previous משנה. It tells us how full it was and how it was covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessel was not just full but heaped above the rim. Because of that, it needed a lid so nothing would spill. A cloth was also laid over it from above to keep in the fragrance.

keyTerms.meaning: Full and heaped: filled above the rim
The incense burned in the היכל
A lid or cover
A cloth covering

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is the tail end of the previous משנה, which was describing the incense vessel.

phrases.english: Full and heaped with incense,
phrases.notes: This is the end of a sentence from the previous משנה about the incense vessel.

phrases.english: and it had a cover.
And a kind of cloth was on it from above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the previous משנה's description of the קטורת vessel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת vessel was heaped full, lidded, and covered with a cloth.

steps.title: The כהן scoops coals from the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. The כהן who won the מחתה takes the silver pan, goes up the outer מזבח, pushes the coals aside, and scoops up well-burned coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who won the coal pan took the silver coal pan and went up to the top of the altar. He pushed the coals to one side and the other, and he scooped from the well-burned inner coals.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the start of a new משנה about the job of the מחתה. It describes the first part: getting coals from the outer מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a silver pan, not gold, for this first step. He clears the coals aside so that he can reach the deep, fully burning coals. Those are the best coals for burning the קטורת inside.

keyTerms.meaning: A coal pan, used to carry burning coals
Won (in the lottery for this job)
Cleared aside
Scooped up coals

phrases.english: The one who won the coal pan,
took the silver coal pan
and went up to the top of the altar,
and cleared the coals to here and to there,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added by the corrected wording, so read it as "this way and that way."

phrases.english: and scooped (from the well-burned inner coals).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה and a new job in the order of the עבודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן of the מחתה scoops well-burned coals from the outer מזבח with a silver pan.

steps.title: Pouring into the gold pan and sweeping the spilled coals
steps.stepSummary: The כהן comes down and pours the coals into the gold pan. About a קב of coals spills, and it is swept into the courtyard's water channel.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came down and poured the coals into the gold pan. About a קב of coals spilled from it, and he would sweep them into the channel.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the same job. It explains how the coals move from the silver pan to the gold pan, and what happens to the extra coals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silver pan held more than the gold one. That is why about one קב spilled when he poured. On a normal day, those spilled coals were swept into the אמה, the channel of water in the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: He poured them out (from one vessel into another)
A measure of volume
Sweeps them
Here: the water channel running through the courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read אמה here as the measurement of a cubit. In this line it means the water channel in the courtyard.

phrases.english: He went down and emptied them into the one of gold,
phrases.notes: "The one of gold" means the gold coal pan.

phrases.english: about a kav of coals scattered from it,
and he would sweep them into the channel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the job of the מחתה, from the silver pan to the gold pan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The coals are moved into the gold pan, and the spilled coals are swept into the אמה.

steps.title: On שבת the spilled coals are covered with a פסכתר
steps.stepSummary: On שבת the spilled coals are not swept into the water. Instead they are covered with a פסכתר, a huge vessel that has two chains.
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבת he would turn a פסכתר upside down over them. The פסכתר was a large vessel that held a לתך. It had two chains. With one, he would pull it and go down. The other was held from above so that it would not roll.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a different rule for שבת. Then it stops to describe what the פסכתר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sweeping coals into water would put them out, and that is not allowed on שבת. So they were just covered. The two chains show the vessel's usual job, carrying ashes down the ramp. One כהן pulled it down while another held it from above so it would not roll.

keyTerms.meaning: Turns a vessel upside down over something
A large vessel used for ashes
A large measure, half a כור
Chains
It would roll

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even in the מקדש, where many שבת rules are set aside for the עבודה, this extra step of sweeping the coals into the water was changed on שבת.

phrases.english: And on Shabbat he would overturn a pesakhter upon them.
And a pesakhter was a large vessel
holding a letekh.
phrases.notes: A לתך is half a כור, a very large amount.

phrases.english: And it had two chains,
one by which he pulls it and goes down,
and one that he holds from above,
so that it would not roll.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the שבת version of what to do with the spilled coals from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת the spilled coals are covered with a פסכתר instead of being swept into the אמה.

steps.title: The three uses of the פסכתר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three jobs of the פסכתר. It covered the spilled coals, it covered a שרץ on שבת, and it carried the ashes down from the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was used for three things: they would turn it over on the coals, and over a שרץ on שבת, and they would take the ashes down from the מזבח in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends this topic by summing up everything the פסכתר was used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of its uses were covering things on שבת: the coals, and a dead שרץ found in the מקדש. Its everyday job was carrying the דשן down from the מזבח. That everyday job is why it had the two chains.

keyTerms.meaning: It is used for
A dead creeping creature, which makes things טמא
The ashes removed from the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן of the מחתה scoops coals with a silver pan and pours them into a gold pan. The spilled coals are swept into the אמה, but on שבת they are covered with the פסכתר. The פסכתר had three uses: covering coals, covering a שרץ on שבת, and carrying down the דשן.

phrases.english: And it served three purposes:
they overturn it upon coals,
and upon a creeping animal on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹרִידִין בָּהּ אֶת הַדֶּשֶׁן מֵעַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: and they take the ashes down from atop the altar in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the uses of the vessel that was described in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסכתר had three uses: covering coals, covering a שרץ on שבת, and carrying down the דשן.

steps.title: The shovel is thrown with a huge noise
steps.stepSummary: Between the אולם and the מזבח, one כהן throws the מגרפה down. It is so loud that nobody in ירושלים can hear anyone else talk.
steps.simpleTranslation: They reached the space between the אולם and the מזבח. One of them took the shovel and threw it down there. No one in ירושלים could hear his friend's voice because of the sound of the shovel.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה continues the order of the morning service. The כהנים reach the space between the אולם and the מזבח, and one of them throws the מגרפה to make a very loud sound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stresses how loud the noise was: it drowned out talking all over ירושלים. That loudness is the whole point, because the next lines explain that the sound worked as a signal.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance hall in front of the היכל
The outer altar in the courtyard
A shovel or rake used in the מקדש; here it is thrown to make a loud noise
The voice of his friend

phrases.english: They reached between the Entrance Hall and the altar,
phrases.notes: The ו just marks this as the sixth משנה. 'They' are the כהנים carrying the קטורת and the coals.

phrases.english: one of them took the shovel
and threw it between the Entrance Hall and the altar.
No person could hear the voice of his friend
in Jerusalem because of the sound of the shovel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the order of the service after the coals were placed in the gold pan and the incense was prepared.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Between the אולם and the מזבח, one כהן throws the מגרפה, making a sound heard throughout ירושלים.

steps.title: Three signals given by the shovel's sound
steps.stepSummary: The sound tells כהנים to come bow and tells לוים to come sing. It also tells the ראש המעמד to stand the טמאים at the eastern gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sound served three purposes. A כהן who heard it knew his fellow כהנים were going in to bow, and he ran to come. A לוי who heard it knew his fellow לוים were going in to sing, and he ran to come. And the ראש המעמד would stand the impure people at the eastern gate.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the three jobs of the loud noise from step 6. Each job is a signal to a different group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two jobs follow the same pattern: someone hears it, knows his brothers are going in, and runs to join them. The third job is different. The ראש המעמד does not run in. He places the טמאים at the eastern gate.

keyTerms.meaning: To bow down
A לוי
To say the song (the לוים' singing)
The head of the group of non-כהנים who stood in the courtyard for the people
People who are ritually impure
The eastern gate

steps.whatToRemember: One loud throw of the מגרפה gave three signals: כהנים come to bow, לוים come to sing, and the טמאים are lined up at the eastern gate.

phrases.english: And it served three purposes:
a priest who hears its sound
knows that his brothers the priests
are going in to bow down, and he runs and comes.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֶן לֵוִי שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹמֵעַ אֶת קוֹלָהּ,
phrases.english: And a Levite who hears its sound
knows that his brothers the Levites

phrases.aramaic: נִכְנָסִים לְדַבֵּר בַּשִּׁיר, וְהוּא רָץ וּבָא.
phrases.english: are going in to say the song, and he runs and comes.
And the head of the מעמד

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מַעֲמִיד אֶת הַטְּמֵאִים בְּשַׁעַר הַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.english: would stand the impure ones at the eastern gate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the purposes of the loud sound described in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sound of the מגרפה signaled כהנים to come bow, לוים to come sing, and the ראש המעמד to stand the טמאים at the eastern gate.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אמר להם הממונה
steps.stepSummary: The closing line marks the end of פרק אמר להם הממונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אמר להם הממונה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line at the end of a פרק. It is not part of the משנה's content.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is named after the פרק's opening words, 'אמר להם הממונה'. It tells the learner that a new פרק starts right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the closing formula at the end of a פרק
The officer in charge of the כהנים

phrases.english: We will return to you,
'The appointee said to them'
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of the פרק, which is how the פרק gets its name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק that ended with step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק אמר להם הממונה is complete.

steps.title: Climbing the steps of the entrance hall
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens as the כהנים start going up the steps of the אולם. The כהנים who won the cleaning of the inner מזבח and the מנורה go ahead of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They began going up the steps of the אולם. Those who had won the cleaning of the inner מזבח and the מנורה would go ahead of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins, picking up the service where the last one stopped. It sets up the order of who enters the היכל first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the קטורת is brought in, two other כהנים must go in first. These are the ones who cleaned the inner מזבח and the מנורה earlier. The משנה is preparing to describe what each of them does inside.

keyTerms.meaning: The steps leading up to the אולם
They won (the job, through the lottery)
Clearing away ashes
The inner (golden) altar inside the היכל
The candelabrum

phrases.english: They began going up the steps of the Entrance Hall.
phrases.notes: The א marks the first משנה of the new פרק. 'They' are still the כהנים with the קטורת and the coals.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁזָּכוּ בְּדִישּׁוּן מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי וְהַמְּנוֹרָה
phrases.english: Those who won the clearing of ashes of the inner altar and the Menorah
would go ahead of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק, continuing the service right after the throw of the מגרפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As the כהנים climb the steps of the אולם, the ones who cleaned the inner מזבח and the מנורה go in ahead of them.

steps.title: The כהן of the inner altar takes his basket
steps.stepSummary: The כהן who cleaned the inner מזבח goes in, takes the basket, bows, and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who won the cleaning of the inner מזבח went in, took the basket, bowed, and left.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now describes the first of the two כהנים from step 9. It lists exactly what he does inside the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His job here is short: he takes back the טני (basket) and bows on the way out. The other כהן, the one for the מנורה, is described next.

keyTerms.meaning: A basket (used for the ashes of the inner altar)
He entered
And he bowed down

phrases.english: The one who won the clearing of ashes of the inner altar
entered and took the basket,
and he bowed down and went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Details the job of the first of the two כהנים introduced in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן of the inner מזבח enters, takes the טני, bows, and leaves.

steps.title: Cleaning the מנורה and keeping the western lamp lit
steps.stepSummary: The כהן cleaning the מנורה finds the two western lamps burning. He cleans the eastern one and leaves the western one lit. If it went out, he relights it from the outer מזבח. Then he takes the jug, bows, and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן who won the cleaning of the מנורה went in and found the two western lamps still burning. He cleaned the more eastern of the two and left the western one burning, because the מנורה was lit from it in the afternoon. If he found it had gone out, he cleaned it and lit it from the outer מזבח. He took the jug from the second step of the stone in front of the מנורה, bowed, and left.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now tells us what the second כהן, the one cleaning the מנורה, does inside the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most lamps are cleaned, but the western lamp is left burning on purpose so the afternoon lighting can come from it. If it went out, the fire to relight it must come from the outer מזבח. Picking up the jug finishes the job he left half done earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Cleaning out the old wicks and ashes of the מנורה
The western lamp, which is left burning
Afternoon, the time of the evening service
The outer מזבח, where the burnt offerings are brought
A jug or pitcher used for the מנורה work

phrases.english: The one who won the cleaning of the מנורה
went in and found
the two western lamps burning.
He cleans the eastern one,
and leaves the western one burning,
because from it he would light
the מנורה in the afternoon.
If he found that it had gone out,
he cleans it and lights it from the outer מזבח.
He took the jug from the second step,
and he bowed and left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the inner מזבח כהן finishes in step 10, the משנה turns to the second כהן mentioned in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clean the eastern of the two western lamps and leave the western one burning. If it went out, relight it from the outer מזבח.

steps.title: Spreading the coals on the inner מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The כהן who won the מחתה piles the coals on the inner מזבח, flattens them with the bottom of the pan, bows, and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן who won the coal pan piled the coals on top of the מזבח, flattened them with the bottom of the pan, bowed, and left.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה describes the כהן who brings the burning coals for the קטורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The coals have to be spread out evenly so the קטורת can be put on them in the next step. This job sets up the burning of the קטורת.

keyTerms.meaning: Coal pan used to carry burning coals
Piled up
Burning coals
Flattened them, spread them out evenly

phrases.english: (Mishnah 2) The one who won the coal pan

phrases.aramaic: צָבַר אֶת הַגֶּחָלִים עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: piled the coals on top of the מזבח,
phrases.notes: This is the inner, golden מזבח inside the היכל.

phrases.english: and flattened them with the bottom of the coal pan,
and he bowed and left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next כהן in line. This is the same כהן of the מחתה from steps 2-3, who now places the coals he brought on the inner מזבח to prepare for the קטורת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The coals are piled on the inner מזבח and flattened with the bottom of the pan.

steps.title: Getting the קטורת ready and the safety warning
steps.stepSummary: The כהן who won the קטורת takes the small vessel out of the spoon and hands it to a friend or relative. Any spilled קטורת is handed to him in handfuls. He is warned to start on the far side so he won't get burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן who won the קטורת would take the small vessel out of the spoon and give it to his friend or relative. If some of it spilled into the spoon, the helper gives it to him by handfuls. They teach him: Be careful not to start in front of you, so you don't get burned.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה describes the כהן who burns the קטורת, starting with how he gets ready and the warning he is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קטורת sits in a small vessel inside a spoon, and a helper holds it for him. No קטורת is wasted: whatever spilled is handed over in handfuls. The warning is practical. If he starts with the side near him, he will have to reach over the burning קטורת.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense burned on the inner מזבח
A small vessel holding the קטורת
A large spoon or ladle that the בזך sits in
Two cupped handfuls
You will be burned

steps.confusionAlert: Two vessels are mentioned. The כף is the outer spoon, and the בזך is the small vessel inside it that holds the קטורת. The spill is from the בזך into the כף.

phrases.english: (Mishnah 3) The one who won the incense

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה נוֹטֵל אֶת הַבָּזֵךְ מִתּוֹךְ הַכַּף,
phrases.english: would take the small vessel out of the spoon,
and give it to his friend or his relative.
If some was scattered from it into it,
phrases.notes: Some קטורת spilled from the small vessel into the spoon.

phrases.english: he gives it to him in his handfuls.
And they teach him:
Be careful in case you begin in front of you,
phrases.notes: Start on the far side of the מזבח, not the side closest to you.

phrases.english: so that you are not burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the coals are spread out, the משנה turns to the כהן who puts the קטורת on them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת is handed over carefully, nothing spilled is lost, and the כהן starts on the far side to avoid burns.

steps.title: Spreading the קטורת and waiting for the command
steps.stepSummary: The כהן spreads the קטורת and leaves. He may not burn it until the ממונה says, "Burn!" If it is the כהן גדול, the ממונה speaks to him respectfully.
steps.simpleTranslation: He began flattening it and would leave. The one burning the קטורת would not burn it until the ממונה told him, "Burn!" And if it was the כהן גדול, the ממונה said to him, "My master, כהן גדול, burn!"
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the spreading of the קטורת and adds that the burning starts only when the ממונה gives the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the כהן גדול does not act on his own. He waits for the ממונה's command. What changes for the כהן גדול is only the respectful wording, "אישי כהן גדול". The command itself still has to be given.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who burns the קטורת
The appointed officer in charge of the service
Burn! The command to burn the קטורת
My master, a respectful way of speaking

steps.whatToRemember: Each job inside the היכל has its own כהן: the inner מזבח, the מנורה, the coals, and the קטורת. The קטורת is burned only when the ממונה commands it, and the כהן גדול is addressed with special respect.

phrases.english: He began flattening it and would leave.
The one burning the incense would not burn it
until the appointed officer says to him: Burn!
And if it was the High Priest,
the appointed officer says to him:
"My master, High Priest, burn!"

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הָיָה הַמַּקְטִיר מַקְטִיר עַד שֶׁהַמְמוּנֶּה אוֹמֵר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the same קטורת כהן, from getting ready to actually burning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת is burned only when the ממונה says to. A כהן גדול is told respectfully, "אישי כהן גדול, הקטר".

steps.title: The people step back and the כהן burns the קטורת
steps.stepSummary: After the signal, the people move away, and the כהן burns the קטורת, bows, and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people stepped away, and he burned the קטורת, bowed, and went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the קטורת service. Everyone steps back, and the כהן burns the קטורת, bows, and leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 taught that the קטורת may not be burned until the ממונה says "Burn!" Now the burning happens. First the people move away, and only then does the כהן burn the קטורת. He finishes the same way the other כהנים did in steps 10-12: he bows and goes out.

keyTerms.meaning: They separated, stepped away
The people (here, those standing nearby)
He burned the קטורת
He bowed down

steps.whatToRemember: The קטורת is burned only after the ממונה's signal and only once the people have stepped away. Then the כהן bows and leaves, just like the other כהנים.

phrases.english: The people withdrew,
and he burned the incense, bowed, and went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the sequence from step 14. The waiting for the ממונה's command ends, and the burning actually happens.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the people step away, the כהן burns the קטורת, bows, and leaves.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter הֵחֵלּוּ עוֹלִים
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing formula marks the end of the פרק הֵחֵלּוּ עוֹלִים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הֵחֵלּוּ עוֹלִים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not a new teaching. It is the traditional line said at the end of a פרק, closing the chapter הֵחֵלּוּ עוֹלִים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן formula means "we will return to you." It shows love for the learning and a wish to come back to it. The chapter's name comes from its opening words, "הֵחֵלּוּ עוֹלִים" ("they began to go up").

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
"They began to go up": the name of the chapter, taken from its first words

steps.whatToRemember: The service of cleaning the מזבח and מנורה and offering the קטורת is now complete, and the פרק ends here.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "They began to go up"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final step of the קטורת service.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק הֵחֵלּוּ עוֹלִים is complete.
